title: Which of two phone plans is cheaper over a year
summary: Plan A wins for heavy data users; Plan B wins under about 1.9 GB of overage per month in this example.

blocks.eyebrow: Example usage, not a carrier quote
blocks.title: Flat rate vs cheap base plus overage
blocks.body: Plan A is $45/mo flat. Plan B is $30/mo plus $8 for every GB over the included allotment. The cheaper plan depends on how many overage gigabytes you actually burn.

columns.name: Plan A — $45/mo flat
columns.detail: $540 per year. No overage meter. Predictable bill even on a travel month.

columns.name: Plan B — $30/mo + $8/GB overage
columns.detail: $360 per year before overage. Each overage GB costs $8. Break-even vs A is $180/year of overage, or 22.5 GB/year (~1.9 GB/mo).

blocks.heading: Year cost at example overage levels (Plan B)
blocks.caption: Break-even is roughly 1.9 GB of overage per month. Above that, Plan A wins.

blocks.title: How to choose from your own usage
blocks.body: Open last month's bill, find the overage (or hotspot) gigabytes, and place yourself on the table. If you usually sit under 2 GB of overage, Plan B is cheaper in this example. If you spike often, Plan A's flat bill is the cheaper insurance.
